text: only one reason to have no ID. That's to have people that can vote that shouldn't be voting. That's the only reason. If you only want the people to vote that should be voting, you ask for ID. Just like you ask for ID for everything else. You want people to vote that probably shouldn't be voting, so you can get some extra votes. That's the only thing that makes sense. I have to admit that when I learned that in part of the US you can vote without showing an ID, it genuinely baffled me. Because in America you need an ID for basically everything. Buying alcohol, renting a car, getting on a plane, even the phones need some sort of authentication to be used. But choosing the person who runs the country for the next four years, you can just walk in and say your name? That just sounded like nonsense to me. But you know my approach. When something sounds crazy, instead of calling it stupid or corrupt, I normally try to research the subject. Because what if I'm missing something? So what is true? 14 states plus Washington DC require no ID at all for most voters. 36 states do request or require it. California is the big one on the no ID list. There you simply need to be registered with the state. You usually do it once, often automatically, when you are at the DMV getting some documents. You give them your driver's license number or the last four digits of your social security number and that gets checked against government records. And that can pretty much be the only time anyone looks. After that you show up on the election day, say your name, sign and get a ballot. And it is quite possible nobody will check anything. Now before we address Joe Rogan's concern, let me mention this. It seems like voter ID is actually nowhere near as controversial as some social media makes it look. Gallup surveyed whether people are in favor of specifically showing photo ID at the polling place. 84% said yes, including 67% of Democrats. And Pew surveyed an even stricter version. Government issued photo ID and got 83%. So majority of Americans from both parties do support voter ID. Now let's talk about Joe Rogan's concern. If you don't have to show ID, what's stopping somebody from showing up and pretending to be somebody else? And this is where the evidence gets interesting. Because the specific kind of fraud that showing ID is designed to prevent somebody physically showing up pretending to be another voter appears to be extremely rare. Now can we know the exact number? Obviously not. If somebody successfully does it and never gets caught, congratulations, they are not going to appear in the statistics. So I wouldn't tell you that voter impersonation literally never happens, but after years of investigations, court cases and research, there just isn't good evidence that it happens on anything close to the scale required for the whole elections are being stolen because nobody checks ID argument. And then you have the argument from the other side. They say voter ID laws can stop legitimate people from voting, especially poor people and minorities, because not everyone has acceptable ID. And one of the biggest studies on this looked at the nationwide data set containing 1.6 billion observations. It found no negative effect from strict voter ID laws on registration or turnout, including by race, gender, age or political party. Which leaves us somewhere funny. One side says no ID means stolen elections. The data says doesn't seem so. The other side says voter ID stops people from voting. The data also says not really. So overall, both sides seem to make this issue much more dramatic than the evidence suggests. Personally, I still think you should have to show ID to vote. Not because I think America has millions of fraudulent voters. At least I couldn't find evidence of that. For me, the main reason is that it seems to be what most Americans wish. And the second reason is consistency. IDs are already required for a lot of things. At the same time, it would be great if getting an acceptable ID would be a reasonably easy and cheap process. These are my thoughts. What do you guys think?
